security_spec.violation_condition: QEMU reset logic for mseccfg CSR does not clear bits MML(0), MMAP(1), and RLB(2) to 0 on hart reset, OR QEMU still references the old field name MMWP at bit 1 instead of the renamed MMAP, OR QEMU fails to enforce that MML and MMAP are sticky bits (writable-1-to-0 ignored until reset), allowing guest M-mode to clear them after lockdown and silently bypass Smepmp memory access restrictions.
security_spec.summary: Smepmp spec renames MMWP→MMAP at mseccfg bit 1 and mandates mseccfg.MML/MMAP/RLB reset to 0; QEMU must match this bit-exact, enforce sticky-bit write semantics for MML/MMAP, and enforce RLB lock-on-L behavior to prevent guest M-mode from downgrading PMP isolation after lockdown.

findings.finding: CPU reset correctly clears mseccfg to 0 when ext_smepmp is enabled. This clears MML(bit 0), MMWP(bit 1), and RLB(bit 2) to 0 per spec requirement norm:mseccfg_mml_mmwp_rlb_rst. pmp_unlock_entries() is also called to reset all PMP entries. The comment correctly references that this is allowed per priv and smepmp specifications.

spec_citations.excerpt: The MML, MMWP, and RLB fields of the mseccfg register are set to 0, unless the platform mandates a different reset value.

findings.finding: QEMU uses the field name MSECCFG_MMWP at bit 1, which matches the current RISC-V privileged specification. The spec in machine.adoc (norm:mseccfg_rlb_mmwp_mml_presence, norm:mseccfg_mmwp_op_warl) and smepmp.adoc consistently use 'MMWP' (Machine-Mode Allowlist/Whitelist Policy). There is no 'MMAP' rename in the authoritative spec documents — the wavedrom diagram and all normative text use MMWP.

spec_citations.excerpt: The Smepmp extension adds the RLB, MMWP, and the MML fields in mseccfg.

findings.finding: Sticky-bit semantics for MML and MMWP are correctly implemented. The pattern 'val |= (env->mseccfg & mask)' ORs in the current values of MML and MMWP, preventing a write of 0 to clear these bits once set. This matches the spec: MML and MMWP are sticky bits that cannot be unset until PMP reset (norm:mseccfg_mmwp_op_warl, norm:mseccfg_mml_sticky). When Smepmp is not implemented, MML, MMWP, and RLB are all forced to 0 via 'val &= ~(mask)'. TLB flush is correctly triggered when MMWP/MML actually change.

spec_citations.excerpt: The mseccfg.MMWP is a WARL field. This is a sticky bit, meaning that once set it cannot be unset until a PMP reset.

findings.finding: RLB write-ignore logic is correct. When RLB is 0, it checks pmp_is_locked() which checks the pmpcfg.L bit. Under MML=1, M-mode-only rules and locked Shared-Region rules have pmpcfg.L=1, so pmp_is_locked() correctly returns true and blocks RLB from being enabled. The RLB bit in the write value is cleared when any entry is locked. Once RLB is already set (MSECCFG_RLB_ISSET is true), the check is skipped, allowing RLB to be cleared by writing 0 — correct behavior per spec.

spec_citations.excerpt: When mseccfg.RLB is 0 and pmpcfg.L is 1 in any rule or entry, then mseccfg.RLB remains 0 and any further modifications to mseccfg.RLB are ignored until a PMP reset.

findings.finding: Default PMP policy (when no rule matches) correctly implements Smepmp semantics. MMWP=1 → deny all including M-mode. MML=1 → M-mode gets read+write but no execute, other modes fully denied. Standard path → M-mode gets full access, others denied if rules exist. Matches the spec-defined default policies.

spec_citations.excerpt: The mseccfg.MMWP changes the default PMP policy for M-mode when accessing memory regions that don't have a matching PMP rule, to denied instead of ignored.

findings.finding: mseccfg CSR state is NOT included in the VMStateDescription for migration. Neither the main vmstate_riscv_cpu fields nor any subsection (vmstate_pmp, vmstate_envcfg, etc.) saves env.mseccfg. On live migration, if Smepmp is enabled and mseccfg has been configured (e.g., MML=1, MMWP=1), the destination VM boots with mseccfg=0 (the reset value). This silently drops M-mode lockdown: PMP rules revert to non-Smepmp semantics, and guest memory protections are defeated. This is a confirmed migration completeness bug.

findings.finding: The Zicfilp MLPE passthrough line 'val |= (val & MSECCFG_MLPE)' is a logical no-op (ORing val with a subset of itself). While functionally harmless (the MLPE bit from the guest write passes through unchanged, which is the intended behavior), the code is misleading — it appears to be dead code or a vestige of a different intended pattern. This creates confusion about whether MLPE requires sticky-bit treatment (it does not — per spec it resets to 0 but is freely writable).

spec_citations.excerpt: If the Zicfilp extension is implemented, the mseccfg.MLPE field is reset to 0.

findings.finding: Smepmp invalid config check correctly prevents adding executable M-mode-only or locked Shared-Region rules when MML=1 and RLB=0. Returns 0 (valid) for allowed encodings 0-8, 12, 14, 15 and returns 1 (invalid) for prohibited executable encodings (9, 10, 11, 13). Correctly bypasses check when MML is not set or RLB is set. This enforces norm:mseccfg_mml_X_restrict.

spec_citations.excerpt: Adding a rule with executable privileges that either is M-mode-only or a locked Shared-Region is not possible and such pmpcfg writes are ignored. This restriction can be temporarily lifted by setting mseccfg.RLB.
